title: Episode 001 with David Choe and Asa Akira
summary: The first DVDASA episode defines the title, cast chemistry and editorial problem the later archive inherits. David Choe and Asa Akira introduce the show as an honesty experiment, with Yoshi Obayashi as comedian, friend and janitor and Bobby NAMBLA operating trivia. David recounts meeting Yoshi after Thumbs Up!, receiving pornography, seeing his confrontational comedy and visiting an early all-Asian American pornography production where he met Asa. Asa describes prior radio work under Akira and Show Whore, the first meeting, her recent marriage to Toni Ribas, relationship boundaries and the effect of marriage on her public image and work. The hosts use an alleged distant family relation as an incest-radio joke; it is not evidence of sexual contact. Much of the episode is explicit pornography-industry conversation: gangbang and blowbang distinctions, performer labor, Nuru massage, public-sex videos, disability fetishization, transgender performers, testing practices, double penetration and Asa Akira Is Insatiable. Statements are personal accounts, jokes, period industry lore or disputed generalizations—not medical, legal or universal sexual guidance. Condom sabotage is introduced as a joke called open-condom style and explicitly said to have been invented in conversation; it must never be converted into instructions. Violent statements about needing to overpower women and hitting a stepmother are source claims requiring attribution, not endorsed advice or established legal fact. References to children encountering pornography and hypothetical teenage sex describe the speakers' anxiety about internet exposure; they must not be excerpted as sexual material involving minors. The transgender discussion uses repeated dated slurs and inaccurate generalizations about bodies, hormones, menstruation, HIV risk and identity. Those words remain in the transcript as historical source speech but do not become archive taxonomy. David's long adolescent masturbation story is autobiographical and contains a private family/home history; it is preserved without constructing an identifying trail. The closing pivots to Asa's awards, authorship ambitions, a candid but time-bound view of marriage, and trivia about Homeland, 24 and cast mannerisms. The episode ends cleanly with thanks and a prerecorded yoga parody.
